about: El Enemigo is the project of two friends: Alejandro “Ale” Vigil, chief winemaker of Catena Zapata, and historian Adrianna Catena, youngest daughter of Nicolás Catena. They started it in 2008 under the name Bodega Aleanna. The name comes from their shared conviction that “we are our own worst enemy”: the real struggle in making wine, as in life, is with your own fears and limits. Guests in Mendoza can visit Vigil’s home winery, Casa Vigil in Chachingo, Maipú, which is themed around Dante’s Divine Comedy.

The 2022 Malbec comes from high-altitude vineyards in Gualtallary, in the Tupungato district of the Uco Valley, at about 1,470 metres on deep, stony, calcareous soils. About a tenth of the blend is Cabernet Franc, Vigil’s signature grape, for freshness and aromatic lift. Fermentation uses native yeasts, with a long, gentle infusion on the skins afterward. The wine then spends fifteen months split between large old foudres, smaller barrels and tank, which keeps the oak in the background.

Critics have praised the 2022. James Suckling (95 points) noted blackberries, violets, a touch of pepper and a precise, focused palate. Wine Advocate (92 points) found floral and herbal tones over black fruit, with refined tannins and a savory, earthy finish. The importers describe a wine of lift rather than weight: black cherry, plum and dark berries, with chalky tannins that come from the limestone soils of Gualtallary.
facts: Gualtallary, Tupungato, about 1,470 m, calcareous soils
